editorial.headline: KBLI 82912: The Business of Making Credit Information Usable
editorial.standfirst: A credit-information bureau can operate at every business scale, with full foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Credit-information bureau activity is the work of assembling, processing and providing information that others use to assess creditworthiness. Its practical subject matter is credit and employment history relating to individuals, as well as information needed to evaluate an individual or a business. The intended users are financial institutions, retailers and other parties that require a credit assessment. The scope also expressly includes credit-information management institutions and alternative credit-rating activity.

This is therefore an information activity with a consequential commercial purpose: making credit data and other relevant data legible for a credit decision. The record describes institutions or bodies that collect and process credit data and other data in order to produce credit information. The editorial distinction matters. The registered activity is not simply the holding of records; it is the creation and provision of usable credit information for organisations assessing creditworthiness.

The activity is open to Micro, Small, Medium and Large businesses. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach 100% under the national position recorded for this activity. That national openness is supported in the record by Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The scale range is broad, but the activity’s scope remains specific: gathering and processing relevant data to generate credit information, including alternative credit ratings.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the island on a permanent basis, but this activity is recorded as not blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK because, at the Large scale, the OSS risk is Medium-High/High; accordingly, it is not caught by that moratorium. For a founder, the honest position is straightforward: PMA registration is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali record does not show this activity as blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium.
